t: Listen to a talk in an economics class.
Economists usually divide unemployment into three types, and each one has a different cause.
This is the short period when people are between jobs.
Say a graduate is looking for her first position, or someone quits to find a better job.
A certain amount of frictional unemployment is actually a sign of a healthy economy, because it means people feel free to move.
It happens when workers' skills no longer match the jobs that are available.
For example, when a factory installs automated machines, some workers lose their jobs, and if they don't have, say, computer skills, they can't easily find new work.
This kind can last for years.
This is caused by the business cycle.
During a recession, people buy less, so overall demand falls, and companies lay off workers.
The good news is that cyclical unemployment usually goes down when the economy recovers.
So remember: between jobs, skills mismatch, and falling demand.
